> **What this case shows** — the [Welch case](../eeg-bandpower-welch-eegmmidb/index.qmd) *averaged*
> the periodograms of overlapping windows into one spectrum. The **spectrogram** (short-time Fourier
> transform) *keeps* them — a **frequency × time** power matrix that resolves how the spectrum
> evolves. On a real eyes-closed posterior EEG channel (POz) it reproduces `scipy.signal.spectrogram`
> **bit-for-bit** (max |diff| ~**7e-13** over all 129 × 11 cells) once the conventions match. And the
> time-frequency view reveals what the averaged spectrum hides: the alpha rhythm dominates **every**
> one of the 11 windows (peak in 8–13 Hz, median **11.25 Hz**), yet its amplitude **waxes and wanes**
> across the 10 s (**CV ~58%**) — the eyes-closed alpha rhythm breathing.

::: {.callout-tip title="The recipe you'll learn"}
**Workflow** — for the time-resolved spectrum: `spectrogram(pe, channel = c)` → a frequency × time
power matrix (plus `$frequencies`, `$times`).
**Way of thinking** — Welch answers *which* frequencies; the spectrogram answers *which frequencies,
when*. Reach for it when the signal is (or might be) non-stationary — a rhythm that waxes and wanes,
a transition, a transient the averaged spectrum would smear away.
**Ecosystem usage** — `PhysioAnalysis::spectrogram()`; the time-resolved sibling of
`bandPower(method = "welch")`.
:::

## Proposition

On real eyes-closed POz EEG, `spectrogram` reproduces `scipy.signal.spectrogram` bit-for-bit (max
|diff| ~7e-13 over 129 × 11 cells); and the alpha rhythm dominates every window (11/11, median
11.25 Hz) while its power waxes and wanes (CV ~58%).

## Question & goal

**The question is fidelity and dynamics: does the ecosystem's spectrogram equal
`scipy.signal.spectrogram` — and what does the time-frequency view show that the averaged Welch
spectrum cannot?** The goal is a machine-precision certification of the STFT over every cell, and a
read of the alpha rhythm's amplitude dynamics.

## Challenge & approach

Two STFTs agree only if their conventions coincide. The op uses a *symmetric* Hann window, *no*
detrend, density scaling, one-sided doubling, `nperseg = 256`, 50% overlap, `mode = "psd"`. scipy's
spectrogram defaults differ (a Tukey window, `detrend = "constant"`), so we point scipy at the op's
conventions — `get_window("hann", 256, fftbins = False)`, `detrend = False` — and compare the full
matrix.

```
EEG POz (eegmmidb, 160 Hz) → spectrogram → 129 × 11 (freq × time) power matrix
                    vs scipy.signal.spectrogram (symmetric Hann, detrend=False, density, psd) → bit-exact (~7e-13)
                                    alpha peak in 11/11 windows, power CV ~58% → the rhythm breathes
```

## Data

**EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database (eegmmidb, PhysioNet)**: subject **S002**, run **R02
(eyes-closed)**, channel **POz** (posterior), first 10 s at 160 Hz — the same git-tracked root the
[Welch](../eeg-bandpower-welch-eegmmidb/index.qmd) and [Hjorth](../eeg-hjorth-eegmmidb/index.qmd)
cases use. Details in [`artifacts/data_sources.json`](artifacts/data_sources.json).

| Quantity | Value |
|---|--:|
| spectrogram size (freq × time) | **129 × 11** |
| op vs `scipy.signal.spectrogram` (max \|diff\|) | **7e-13** (bit-exact) |
| **median peak frequency (alpha rhythm)** | **11.25 Hz** |
| windows with peak in alpha (8–13 Hz) | **11 / 11** (sustained) |
| **alpha-power CV across time** | **~58%** (waxing/waning) |
| mean alpha power (POz) | **2465** |

The op equals scipy to the FFT floating-point floor across every cell, and the time-frequency view
shows a sustained-yet-modulated alpha rhythm. Values trace to
[`artifacts/spectrogram_summary.csv`](artifacts/spectrogram_summary.csv).

## Conclusion

The ecosystem's spectrogram *is* `scipy.signal.spectrogram` — bit-for-bit over the full matrix, once
the symmetric-Hann + no-detrend + density conventions are pinned — so the time-frequency estimator is
certified against the reference; and on real eyes-closed EEG it shows the posterior alpha rhythm as
sustained (dominant in every window) yet breathing (CV ~58%), cross-consistent with the Welch case's
high posterior alpha power and the Hjorth case's low posterior mobility on the same data. The
transferable takeaway: **use the spectrogram when time matters — it recovers dynamics (waxing,
waning, transitions) that the averaged spectrum smears away — and pin the window, detrend, and
scaling conventions before comparing STFTs across tools.**

## Open questions

- The spectrogram's real power is on **non-stationary** signals — an eyes-open → eyes-closed
  transition (alpha appearing), a fatiguing EMG contraction (the median frequency compressing over
  time), or motor-imagery event-related desynchronization. Running it across such a transition, with
  the per-window frequencies pinned against scipy, would turn the bit-exact estimator into a dynamic
  biomarker. *Documented, not escalated.*

## Using this in your own analysis

| Step | Function | Package |
|---|---|---|
| spectrogram (frequency × time) | `spectrogram()` | PhysioAnalysis |
| averaged spectrum (the sibling view) | `bandPower(method = "welch")` | PhysioAnalysis |
| time-domain complexity | `eegComplexity()` (Hjorth) | PhysioEEG |

**Choosing the parameters.**

- **window_size** — the FFT length per window (here 256 = 1.6 s at 160 Hz); larger gives finer
  frequency but coarser time resolution (the time-frequency trade-off).
- **overlap** — the fraction of overlap between windows (here 0.5); more overlap gives smoother time
  resolution at more compute.
- **window_type** — `"hanning"` (this case, symmetric Hann) tapers each segment to control spectral
  leakage.
- **the conventions** — the STFT depends on the window, detrend, scaling, and overlap; pin them
  before comparing across tools (scipy's spectrogram defaults — Tukey window, `detrend = "constant"`
  — differ from this op's).

**The recipe, copy-runnable:**

```r
library(PhysioAnalysis)

sg <- spectrogram(pe, channel = 58, window_size = 256, overlap = 0.5)  # POz
image(sg$times, sg$frequencies, t(sg$power))          # the time-frequency map
alpha <- colSums(sg$power[sg$frequencies >= 8 & sg$frequencies <= 13, ])  # alpha over time

# equals scipy.signal.spectrogram bit-for-bit (max |diff| ~7e-13) with matched conventions:
# get_window("hann", 256, fftbins = FALSE), detrend = FALSE, scaling = "density", mode = "psd".
```

**Auditing the numbers.** Every value on this page traces to
[`artifacts/spectrogram_summary.csv`](artifacts/spectrogram_summary.csv), and [`audit.py`](audit.py)
re-checks each number, the bit-exact scipy match over all 129 × 11 cells, the sustained-yet-modulated
